By records: imported exactly 1292, with caveats 351, not imported 1759 (of 3402).

Caveats (cards may carry several), with their direction: does the term allow outcomes the printed card does not (allows more), forbid outcomes it allows (forbids some), or both? A card imported with caveats is in general neither an over- nor an under-approximation of its printed card, so the imported pool must not be used for "no deck can ..." arguments without checking the caveat.

| caveat | direction | cards | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upTo0` | allows more | 20 | 'up to N' in a Trainer or an Ability allows 0 in the model; today's rule asks for at least 1 outside attacks (Known gaps, S8 PP26) |
| `noopUse` | allows more | 19 | an Ability whose effect may do nothing in the model (a switch with an empty Bench, a heal of an undamaged Pokémon, a move of Energy that moves none, a take when there is nothing to take, a condition tested when the effect resolves) can be used to no effect, marking its Pokémon as used; whether the printed game allows such a use was not checked |
| `mayFail` | allows more | 10 | an attach or Bench placement may do nothing in the model (`attach` and `putBench` always allow nothing), a superset of the printed 'attach a …' from the hand or discard pile, and of 'if you can' (Known gaps) |
| `aceSpec` | allows more | 8 | the ACE SPEC deck-building limit is not modelled (no deck construction in the model) |
| `hiddenInfo` | allows more | 6 | a sentence that only reveals or looks at cards is a no-op (hidden information is not modelled, Known gaps) |
| `noopPlay` | allows more | 6 | a Trainer whose effect may do nothing in the model (switch with an empty Bench, heal an undamaged Pokémon, cure a Pokémon with no Special Condition) can be played to no effect; a Trainer cannot be played when its effect cannot happen (taken from rulings, not in the 2023 rulebook on hand) |
| `searchAny` | allows more | 4 | a deck search for 'a card' (any card) may find nothing in the model |
| `moveAnyPair` | allows more | 2 | a move of Energy printed between particular Pokémon ('to this Pokémon', 'from 1 of your Benched Pokémon to your Active Pokémon') is a move between any two of the player's Pokémon (moveEnergy) |
| `selfBench` | allows more | 2 | 'this Pokémon' on the Bench is one Benched Pokémon chosen when the effect resolves, and for an on-play Ability the Active Pokémon or a Benched one (Known gaps, M8a: SelfOp.at) |
| `onePerName` | allows more | 1 | 'You can't use more than 1 X Ability each turn' is not modelled: the use flag is per Pokémon, so each of several Pokémon with that Ability can use it in the same turn |
| `perPokemon` | both | 80 | a lingering effect printed on one Pokémon ('this Pokémon', 'the Defending Pokémon') is a modifier of its player in the model (Known gaps: modifiers belong to a player) |
| `recoil` | both | 62 | self-damage ('also does N damage to itself') is written as damage counters (selfDamage): no Weakness, Resistance or modifier applies to it (Known gaps) |
| `benchMods` | both | 41 | attack damage to Benched Pokémon takes no bonus, reduction or prevention in the model (Known gaps, milestone M3) |
| `staticBench` | both | 12 | a static damage reduction ('takes N less damage from attacks') is subtracted at step 5 of the damage calculation, which only damage to the Active Pokémon passes through: attack damage to a Benched Pokémon takes no reduction in the model (Known gaps, milestone M3: Bench damage takes no bonus, reduction or prevention; milestone M6) |
| `poisonStrength` | both | 1 | a stronger Poison ('N damage counters instead of 1') is written as Poison plus poisonUp (N-1); the Known gaps list numbered Poison variants as absent |

Stacking texts ("The effect of X doesn't stack", "You can't apply more than 1 … at a time") in static Abilities: 6, all refused. The model adds every static effect in force, so two Pokémon with the Ability give twice the amount, where the printed card gives it once: a different HP, damage or reduction, which changes outcomes in both directions (more HP lets a Pokémon survive what the printed card Knocks Out, and a larger bonus Knocks Out what the printed card leaves standing), so the term would not be an over-approximation and an "allows more" caveat would be false. Pokémon Tools and Stadiums in the pool print no stacking text (a player has one Stadium in play; one Tool per Pokémon).

- Bouffalant (svp-136): "As long as you have at least 1 other Bouffalant in play, all of your Basic Colorless Pokémon take 60 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). The effect of Curly Wall doesn't stack." Refused; without the stacking sentence the rest is refused too (cond).
